question: What should I inspect or document before moving into an apartment?

requiredPoints.source: Chapter 1: prepare a statement describing the condition of the apartment. This is called a "Statement of Condition." ... You may want to take pictures (or video) of certain conditions.

question: Can a landlord use an old eviction record against me during tenant screening?

requiredPoints.source: Handout 2: Starting in May 2025, there will be a process to seal an eviction.

question: When does a landlord have to return my security deposit after I move out?

requiredPoints.source: Handout 3: the landlord must return your security deposit balance, with interest, within 30 days after you move out.

question: What is the difference between a lease and a tenancy at will?

requiredPoints.point: a lease runs for a set time
requiredPoints.source: Handout 4: Tenant with Lease: If you have a written agreement to rent for a specific time period at a specific rent ...

requiredPoints.point: a tenancy at will runs month to month
requiredPoints.source: Handout 4: If your agreement with your landlord is a month-to-month tenancy, you are a tenant at will.

question: Can my landlord raise my rent whenever they want?

requiredPoints.source: Handout 5: Your landlord can only raise the rent if they give you proper notice and you agree to the increase.

question: My landlord shut off heat and hot water. What can I do?

requiredPoints.source: Handout 6: If you cannot reach the landlord or they do not fix the problem, call the local Board of Health.

question: Is it illegal for a landlord to discriminate against families with children?

requiredPoints.source: Handout 7 lists as illegal discrimination: You have young children, and a landlord tells you they cannot rent to you because the apartment has lead paint.

question: When can a tenant withhold rent because serious repairs were not made?

requiredPoints.point: the landlord must know about the problems first
requiredPoints.source: Chapter 8: Does the landlord know about the defective conditions (and know this before you were behind in your rent)?

question: What must a landlord do if a child under 6 lives in a unit with lead paint?

requiredPoints.point: remove or cover the lead hazards
requiredPoints.source: Handout 9: property owners must remove or cover all lead paint hazards in homes built before 1978 where any children under 6 live.

question: Can tenants organize together without the landlord retaliating against them?

requiredPoints.source: Chapter 10: an adverse action, such as notice to quit or a rent increase, within six months of organizing or joining a tenants' union is presumed retaliation.

question: What should I do before moving out to protect my security deposit?

requiredPoints.source: Handout 11: Take pictures before you leave.

question: What is a notice to quit in an eviction case?

requiredPoints.point: you need not leave until a court orders it
anyOf: does not mean you must move
requiredPoints.source: Handout 12: You do not have to move out by the date on a Notice to Quit. ... The number of days is the "notice period" and tells you how long you have before your landlord can go to court.

question: Can I take my landlord to court over bad housing conditions?

requiredPoints.source: Handout 13: Landlords must provide "habitable" or decent living conditions. You can ask the court to order them to make repairs and return part of your rent.

question: How does the Massachusetts court process work for a tenant civil case?

requiredPoints.source: Handout 14: most landlord-tenant cases in Housing Court or District Court. If there is a Housing Court where you live, consider starting your case there.

question: Do tenants in rooming houses have special rights?

requiredPoints.point: protection grows with time lived there
requiredPoints.source: Handout 15: If you have lived in the rooming house 30 days or less ... More than 30 days ... More than 3 months: the type of notice depends on the reason for eviction.

question: What rights do mobile home park residents have?

requiredPoints.source: Handout 16: The rules the park owner makes must be approved by the Attorney General's Office ... A park owner cannot: Evict you unless they get a court order.

question: What rights do tenants have if their building is being converted to condos?

requiredPoints.source: Handout 17: they must give you a notice to vacate at least 1 year before the date they want you to move out ... at least 2 years if you have a limited income, are 62 years or older, or have a physical disability.

question: What rights do tenants have after a foreclosure?

requiredPoints.point: the new owner cannot make you leave without just cause and a court order
requiredPoints.source: Handout 18: You only need to move out if a court orders you to leave. ... can usually only be evicted for “just cause”

RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT
This lease is between the Landlord and Tenant for the apartment at 12 Beacon Street, Boston, MA.
1. Term and Renewal: This lease runs for one year. The Tenant must give the Landlord at least 60 days written notice before the end of the term to renew.
2. Rent: Monthly rent is $1,800, due on the first of each month.
3. Repairs: The Landlord must repair heating, plumbing, and electrical problems within 48 hours of written notice.
4. Security Deposit: The Landlord holds a $1,800 security deposit and will return it within 60 days after move-out, minus any itemized deductions.
5. Late Fee: A late fee of $50 applies if rent is paid after the 5th of the month.

question: Can my landlord come into my apartment whenever they want without asking me first?

requiredPoints.point: permission, an emergency or a court order
requiredPoints.source: Chapter 1: The landlord is only allowed to enter your apartment if you give them permission, if it is an emergency, or if they have a court order.

question: Can my landlord charge me a late fee if I pay my rent five days late?

requiredPoints.point: no late fee until 30 days late
requiredPoints.source: Handout 5: your landlord cannot collect the late fee until 30 days after the rent was due.

question: My landlord changed the locks while I was at work. Is that allowed?

requiredPoints.source: Handout 12: To evict you, a landlord must get permission from a court to force you to leave your rented apartment or home. They can't lock you out.

question: Can a landlord refuse to rent to me because I have a Section 8 voucher?

requiredPoints.source: Handout 7 lists as illegal discrimination: A landlord refuses to rent to you because you have a Section 8 voucher.

question: Does my landlord have to pay me interest on my security deposit?

requiredPoints.source: Handout 3: Pay you interest on your security deposit and last month's rent once a year.

question: Can my landlord evict me because I reported bad conditions to the Board of Health?

requiredPoints.source: Chapter 12: If a landlord sends you a Notice to Quit or tries to evict you by going to court within 6 months after you did any of the activities protected by the law, a judge must "presume" that your landlord is retaliating.

requiredPoints.source: Booklet 10: File an Affidavit of Indigency. Tell the court you cannot afford the fees and costs in your case, and ask the court to waive your court fees.
